evidenceAudit.scope: Recognition and emergency treatment of anaphylaxis in adults and children in Indian hospitals and clinics: intramuscular adrenaline, airway, fluids, refractory anaphylaxis, observation, discharge and allergy referral, using the World Allergy Organization (WAO) Anaphylaxis Guidance 2020 and the Resuscitation Council UK (RCUK) 2021 guideline because no Indian national anaphylaxis guideline was found.
findings: Definition, two clinical criteria and IM adrenaline doses (0.01 mg/kg, maximum 0.5 mg; 0.15 mg for 1–5 years; 0.3 mg for 6–12 years; 0.5 mg for teenagers and adults) checked against WAO 2020.

Anterolateral thigh site, repeat after 5 minutes, refractory pathway after two IM doses, fluid bolus 500–1000 mL in adults and 10 mL/kg in children, positioning, antihistamines as third-line and no routine corticosteroids checked against RCUK 2021 and its algorithm.
unverifiedSections: No Indian national anaphylaxis guideline was found; this topic uses WAO 2020 and RCUK 2021.
IV adrenaline infusion rates for refractory anaphylaxis are not given in the opened sources; use only with specialist (anaesthesia or intensive care unit (ICU)) support.
Glucagon dose for patients on beta-blockers, salbutamol and antihistamine doses are not given in the opened sources and are not dosed here.
Mast cell tryptase timing, its reference value (about 11.4 ng/mL, assay dependent) and observation duration were not in the opened extracts; follow local protocol.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Anaphylaxis is a serious systemic hypersensitivity reaction that is usually rapid in onset and may cause death (WAO 2020). Mast-cell and basophil mediators cause vasodilatation, capillary leak, bronchospasm and upper-airway oedema. Common triggers in India are drugs (antibiotics, NSAIDs, contrast), insect stings and foods. Intramuscular adrenaline into the anterolateral thigh is the first and most important treatment; there is no absolute contraindication to it (WAO 2020). Antihistamines and corticosteroids do not treat airway, breathing or circulation problems and must never delay adrenaline (RCUK 2021).
keyMechanisms: IgE-mediated or direct mast-cell activation releases histamine, tryptase and leukotrienes.
Vasodilatation and capillary leak cause distributive shock.
Bronchial smooth-muscle contraction and laryngeal oedema obstruct the airway.
Adrenaline reverses these through alpha and beta receptors.

symptoms: Sudden itch, flushing, urticaria or angioedema
physicalSigns: Urticaria and angioedema (absent in some cases)
redFlags: Airway swelling, stridor or hoarse voice
No improvement after two IM adrenaline doses: refractory anaphylaxis (RCUK 2021)
precipitants: Antibiotics (beta-lactams), NSAIDs, contrast media, anaesthetic drugs
Foods such as peanut, tree nuts, shellfish

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Bradycardia, pallor, rapid recovery lying flat; no rash or wheeze.
Wheeze without skin signs or hypotension.
Skin only; no airway, breathing or circulation problem.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Acute onset (minutes to hours) of skin and/or mucosal involvement plus involvement of at least one other organ system (respiratory, circulation or gastrointestinal).
Acute hypotension, bronchospasm or laryngeal involvement after exposure to a known or highly probable allergen, even without skin signs.
Respiratory or cardiovascular problems persisting after two doses of IM adrenaline.

clinicalManagement.title: Recognise and call for help
actions: Use WAO criteria; if in doubt, give IM adrenaline (RCUK 2021).
Remove the trigger (stop infusion, remove sting).
Lie flat; sit up if breathing is easier; left side if pregnant; avoid sudden standing (RCUK 2021).

clinicalManagement.title: IM adrenaline
actions: Adrenaline 1 mg/mL into the anterolateral mid-thigh (dose by age, see medicines).
Repeat after 5 minutes if no improvement (RCUK 2021).
High-flow oxygen; monitoring: SpO2, ECG, BP.

clinicalManagement.title: Circulation
actions: Hypotension or shock: IV crystalloid bolus 500–1000 mL in adults, 10 mL/kg in children (RCUK algorithm).
Give fluids early in refractory anaphylaxis (RCUK 2021).

clinicalManagement.title: Refractory anaphylaxis
actions: Seek expert help early; IV adrenaline infusion only in a specialist setting by skilled clinicians (RCUK 2021).
Continue IM adrenaline every 5 minutes until an infusion is running.
Patients on beta-blockers may need glucagon: discuss with a specialist.
Start cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and follow advanced life support.

clinicalManagement.title: After stabilisation
actions: Non-sedating oral antihistamine for persistent skin symptoms; corticosteroids are not routine (RCUK 2021).
Observe before discharge per local protocol.
Refer every patient to an allergy clinic (RCUK 2021).
